rv.q: "Watching 'Talk House,' I had the uncanny sensation that Shawn has turned his theatrical nightmares into our waking reality...Staged with sly humor and creeping perversity by Elliott, 'Talk House' is elliptical, weird stuff. Unless you’re already a fan, you may find it opaque or off-puttingly cryptic.
"The play digests so easily and un-queasily that it can feel like it was barely there at all...'Evening at the Talk House' ought to be a body slam.
A dystopian theater party that never quite gels.
And though overwritten, his play is a shrewdly pointed satire about civilization's tectonic shifts both culturally and politically.

Too bad the play by Wallace Shawn ("The Fever"), who's part of a seven-actor ensemble that includes Matthew Broderick and "L.A. Law" alums Jill Eikenberry and Michael Tucker, doesn't give you that much to chew on.
